clue.text: Fine musical returns, featuring unknown old minx

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: featuring means the turned title includes the unknown inside it
returns tells us to read the musical's name backwards

parts.note: Gigi is the Lerner and Loewe film musical
Z is an algebraic unknown, as x, y and z are

explanation.surface: A critic praises a revived show starring a cheeky young woman of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GIGI into IGIG; 'featuring' sets Z inside it, after the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a flighty, flirtatious girl, which is exactly what a minx is.

clue.text: Python stands up during panel discussion

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
during says the letters sit within the words panel discussion, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A comedian rises to speak while a panel show is being recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ELDI sits inside 'panEL DIscussion'; 'stands up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was one of the Monty Python comedy team, so the surname names a Python.

clue.text: Leave Jules's special teacher at home

parts.note: to leave is to go
Jules Verne, the French novelist, with his possessive

explanation.surface: Someone urges us to quit a French writer's unusual tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to educate children in their own household is a home teacher.

clue.text: Dope and crack for those in estates?

parts.note: dope is slang for information, as is gen
to have a crack at something is to have a try

explanation.surface: Drugs being dealt on housing estates.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests council estates; the definition means country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed class who own country houses and estates, so the question mark flags a playful description.

clue.text: Conservative MP gets in again after changing crusade

indicators.note: gets in means the letters MP are placed inside the reworked letters
the word again is altered, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is re-elected after switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after changing' makes AAIGN, and 'gets in' has it take in the MP; the surface's turncoat MP is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised drive for a cause is a crusade, as in a political or moral push.

clue.text: Writer's sweet Breton confection

parts.note: a charlotte is a pudding of fruit in a mould lined with bread or sponge

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed up, so the letters of Breton are remixed

explanation.surface: A writer's French pastry, made the Breton way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confection' rearranges BRETON into BRONTE.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the novelist who wrote Jane Eyre; this puzzle marks her bicentenary in 2016.

clue.text: Brief affair involving English over old saloon

indicators.note: involving means the shortened word wraps round the turned letters
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an affair is a matter, as in a business affair

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the abbreviation turns upside down

explanation.surface: A fling with an Englishman is finished, the old shop-worn tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' leaves MATTE and 'over' gives GNE, which 'involving' encloses. 'affair' means a matter, not a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The MG Magnette was a British family car of the 1950s, a saloon body style now long out of production.

clue.text: Tax cut oddly reduced working in London area

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of the words tax cut are dropped, keeping the rest

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A tax cut, strangely trimmed, comes into force in part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'Tax cut' leaves ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of west London in the borough of Ealing.

clue.text: Someone staring over edge, touching the end

indicators.note: over means covering, so the starer's letters go round the others

parts.note: a gaper is someone who stares open-mouthed
a rim is an edge
re means concerning, touching on

explanation.surface: A person peering over a precipice, close to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a container signal, not a position: the starer covers the edge. 'touching' gives letters rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooded figure with a scythe personifies death, the final end of life.

clue.text: Small range, one in city state

indicators.note: in places these letters within the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a range is a kitchen stove with an oven
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A small mountain range, one found in a city-state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like mountains but is a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A country in central Europe, formerly part of Yugoslavia, independent since 1991.

clue.text: Style attained height in churches, primarily

parts.note: to have attained something is to have got it

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the words in and churches

explanation.surface: An architectural style reached its height in church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An architectural manner of pointed arches and vaulting, also a later literary mode.

clue.text: Clerical office Harry Lauder ran on English lines

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: The Scottish music-hall singer Harry Lauder managed things the English way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like Lauder's first name but signals the anagram of LAUDERRAN plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A church post, the office of a cleric who supervises a group of parishes.

clue.text: A cargo ship transported old boxes

indicators.note: transported means carried off and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A freighter carried ancient crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone coffins of the ancient world, the boxes in which the dead were placed.

clue.text: Nice setter entertains a new girl

indicators.note: entertains means holds a guest within, so the French pronoun goes round the other letters

parts.note: a setter in Nice, France, would call themself je, French for I

explanation.surface: A pleasant crossword compiler hosts a new young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, here also the heroine of the writer's best-known novel.

clue.text: Class sorts out test cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the test word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: sorts means rearranges, so the letters of out are reordered

explanation.surface: A class sorts through test cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorts' gives UTO and 'cases' wraps the test word round it; 'test cases' reads as legal jargon but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A small teaching session in a college or university is a type of class.

clue.text: Radical old queen hides bust somewhere in Kent

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Radical, the political party

indicators.note: hides means keeps something inside, so the bust goes between the other letters

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a woman's bust is her chest

explanation.surface: An extreme former monarch conceals a sculpture somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Rochester is also the hero of Jane Eyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic cathedral city on the Medway in the county, an example of a place there.

clue.text: Viewer's complaint about diplomacy engaging Arab

parts.note: CA is circa, about, used with dates

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the diplomacy word holds the other letters

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A TV watcher grumbles about a diplomatic approach to an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' looks like a TV watcher; it is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye disease in which the lens clouds over, a complaint of the organ of sight.

clue.text: Ray follows reserve scorer on rink

indicators.note: follows means the fish comes after the reserve word

parts.note: ice means reserve, a cold aloofness of manner
a skate is a flat fish of the ray family

explanation.surface: A footballer called Ray comes after the substitute goalscorer, on an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' means a blade that cuts marks into the ice, not a goalscorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed boot whose runner cuts lines into the frozen surface as the wearer glides.

clue.text: Short division? Sign on staff

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a cleft is a split or division

explanation.surface: A quick sum, then a notice on the workforce board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol at the start of the stave that fixes the pitch of the notes, a musical sign.

clue.text: Did school put rubbish outside that's foul?

indicators.note: put outside means the rubbish word goes round the other letters

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
ugh is an exclamation of disgust at something foul

explanation.surface: Did the school put out bin bags that stank?
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's foul' is an exclamation, not a description of the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to educate them, so schooled and the past tense of teach are synonyms.

clue.text: In which kinky pair agree on hosting male?

definitions.text: In which kinky pair agree on hosting male?

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so the jumbled letters take in the male
kinky means twisted, so the letters of pair agree on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broad-minded couple consent to bringing in another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' gives OPENARRIAGE, which 'hosting' fills with the male. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership in which both spouses agree that either may take other lovers, as the clue pictures.

clue.text: Book half a month online

indicators.note: half of the eight-letter month name is its first four letters

parts.note: November is the eleventh month
read as on line: L for line, placed below in a down entry

explanation.surface: A book published in instalments on the internet for a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' splits as 'on line': L goes under NOVE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A long prose fiction is a kind of book, like the novels this puzzle celebrates.

clue.text: Call law graduate up about drug

indicators.note: about means going round, so the turned letters surround the drug
in a down clue, up means the degree letters read bottom to top

parts.note: LLB is the degree of Bachelor of Laws
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Phone the law graduate about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LLB to BLL, and 'about' puts E after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a bell is British slang for a phone call.

clue.text: Sage, I'm sorry to say, comes back around six

indicators.note: around means the reversed word surrounds the number
comes back means the expression is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an expression of regret
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A wise person regretfully returns at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' gives SALA, which 'around' wraps round the number. 'Sage' looks like a wise person but is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of the herb, so the plant name stands for the herb itself.

clue.text: Getting warm neckwear and dark clothing?

parts.note: in guessing games, getting warm means getting near, nigh
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Putting on scarves and dark clothes as it gets warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark' means night-time, not a sombre colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn to bed, so clothing for after dark; the question mark flags the playful wording.

clue.text: Old person from Riga features in odious 21

indicators.note: features in means appears inside, so the Latvian goes into the odious word

parts.note: odious means vile
a Lett is an old word for a Latvian, and Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: An old Latvian appears in a nasty book.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer of clue 21, a book; 'features in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel by the same writer, published in 1853, so it is an example of the book type.

clue.text: Dominate high-scoring draw without central pairing

indicators.note: the two letters at the middle of the score are taken away

parts.note: three-all is a high score in a drawn football match

explanation.surface: Win a high-scoring tied match without the central partnership in place.
explanation.walkthrough: THREE-ALL loses its middle EE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in bondage or subjection is to dominate them, an old verb sense.
